 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet India have had four days to swap Bengaluru for Christchurch © AFP India have had four days to swap Bengaluru for Christchurch © AFP India have barely unzipped their suitcases this month. The Asian Games assignment in Japan ended on October 3; three days later they were in Lucknow for a five-match series that ran through Ranchi, Indore and Hyderabad before closing in the Bengaluru rain late on October 17. Four days on, they start again in Christchurch, with the jet lag surely travelling with them.
 New Zealand is a tricky tour at the best of times. India come here less often than they go to England or Australia, and a turnaround this short only sharpens the challenge. For Shreyas Iyer, it may feel familiar. He spoke about acclimatisation in his pre-series press conference in Christchurch, and with reason: his tenure began with India out of rhythm in Ireland, where they lost 0-2, before England beat them too.
 It is an occupational hazard of the modern Indian cricketer, and there's a good chance that conditions won’t meet them halfway either. White-ball cricket may have standardized conditions, but early-season New Zealand can still offer a different challenge. The last 200 in this country came nine T20Is ago, a world away from the kind of cricket India have been involved at home.
 When these sides last met, in the T20 World Cup final in Ahmedabad in March, India piled up 255. Much has changed since, not least Iyer’s elevation to the captaincy. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi debuted in Manchester at 15 but has struggled for game time behind World Cup-winning openers. The bowling, meanwhile, has kept reaching for experience, culminating in Bhuvneshwar Kumar’s recall after two excellent IPL seasons with RCB.
 But two lynchpins remain missing. Jasprit Bumrah has been rested with the Test series in mind, and Hardik Pandya hasn’t played international cricket since that night in Ahmedabad. Finding the right balance is India’s first puzzle in Christchurch, and they may have to solve it before their body clocks catch up.
 When: New Zealand vs India, 1st T20I, October 22, 12.30 PM IST, 8:00 PM Local
 Where: Hagley Oval, Christchurch
 What to expect: Evening conditions should be mostly pleasant, though dew could come into play and nudge captains towards chasing. Christchurch produced the highest score of the series earlier this year, South Africa’s 187, but that came at the end of the summer. Early in the season, there could be a little more in it for the seamers.
 Team News: 
 India 
 Varun Chakaravarthy returns after another spell on the sidelines with injury, though fitting him into the XI could be tricky if India opt for three frontline seamers in a season opener. Naman Dhir was the find of the series against West Indies, but he may be the one to make way if India go with two seam-bowling all-rounders in Nitish Reddy and Shivam Dube.
 Probable XI: Sanju Samson (wk), Abhishek Sharma, Ishan Kishan, Shreyas Iyer (c), Tilak Varma, Shivam Dube, Nitish Kumar Reddy, Axar Patel, Bhuvneshwar Kumar, Prince Yadav/Varun Chakaravarthy, Arshdeep Singh
 New Zealand 
 Without Mark Chapman and Rachin Ravindra, the hosts have a top-three spot for Devon Conway. They have as many as six seamers in the squad to pick from, with Glenn Phillips and Michael Bracewell offering part-time spin in a fairly stacked bowling attack.
 Probable XI: Finn Allen, Tim Seifert (wk), Devon Conway, Glenn Phillips, Daryl Mitchell, Michael Bracewell, Mitchell Santner (c), Nathan Smith, Kyle Jamieson, Matt Henry, Lockie Ferguson
 Did You Know? 
 - India have played 21 T20Is post their World Cup win earlier this year - 10 more than the next Full Member side in this period. These 21 T20Is were spread across seven series in five countries.
 - Since January 2020, India have won 16 of the 20 completed matches against New Zealand, including two Super Over wins, with one game ending in a tie.
 - Since October 2024, Jacob Duffy is the fourth highest wicket-taker among seamers in T20Is. He has been exceptional at home in this period, with 36 wickets in 19 matches at an average of 12.72 and an economy of 7.19.
 - Ishan Kishan needs seven more runs to surpass Suryakumar Yadav (1164 runs in 2022) for most runs by an Indian in a calendar year in T20Is.
 What they said: 
 "If we look at the conditions here, fast bowling suits the best. It's not like the conditions are completely different. But when we played in England, they had prepared wickets according to our batting. On a given day, no one knows how the wicket will be, so we'll try to acclimatise as soon as possible. And if we have a good practice session, then every individual will get a fair idea about how to plan." - Shreyas Iyer
